Theme

Travel & transport · Nature & food

southern adjective

also south (as in the south side), southerly, in the south, facing south

classical

Varr. RR 1.7.1: ager spectat ad merīdiānam caelī partem (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 206

merīdiānus, merīdiāna, merīdiānum

Declension on Wiktionary

First “of midday” (merīdiānus somnus, the siesta), and so of the south, where the sun stands at noon (see south). Facing south is in merīdiem spectāre (Cato, below).

Other words

  • austrālis, austrāle — southern

    also used · classical · Cic. N.D. 2.50: aquilōnia tum austrālis; Tusc. 1.68: austrālis ōra (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    From auster, the south wind (see south wind); Cicero’s word for the southern regions of the earth.

  • austrīnus, austrīna, austrīnum — southern, southerly

    also used · classical · Verg. G. 2.271: calōrēs (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    (vōx plērumque poētica: Verg.; also Plin.)

    As a noun, austrīna are the southern parts of a country (Pliny).

  • merīdiōnālis, merīdiōnāle — southern

    also used · late Latin · Lact. 2.9; Firm. Math. 2.12 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 85, 383 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Late (Lactantius, Firmicus); Traupman uses it, but merīdiānus is the classical word.

Examples

  • sī poteris, sub rādīce montis siet, in merīdiem spectet, locō salūbrī

    if you can, let it lie at the foot of a mountain, facing south, in a healthy spotCato Agr. 1.3

  • ager spectat ad merīdiānam caelī partem

    the land faces the southern quarter of the skyVarr. RR 1.7.1 (Lewis & Short)

See also south, south wind, northern.
